target_customer: Teams building AI agents and applications that need runtime security against prompt injection
problem: Input filters miss multi step prompt injection and tool misuse by agents, so harmful actions slip through.
business_model: B2B security SaaS via SDK, four week proof of concept then contract

founders.name: Eduardo Velasco
prior_employers: Amazon (tech lead, low latency ML models)

competitors.name: Superagent Guard
competitors.what: Guardrail classifier between app and model released January 2026

competitors.name: Capsule Security
competitors.what: Runtime security for AI agents, emerged from stealth April 2026

technical_complexity.rationale: Low latency trajectory classification with an automated attack discovery and retraining loop is hard ML and security work for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: Verified exploit data feeding retraining could compound, but benchmarks are self reported and many funded rivals exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Several security vendors shipped runtime agent protection in the first half of 2026; no acquisition of Silmaril found.

market_need_then: Agent adoption and prompt injection incidents drove security spend in 2026. Company claims of 96 percent block rate and $28M damages stopped are unverified; the website quotes a different damages figure.

branding.name_origin: Appears to reference Tolkien's Silmarils (jewels of captured light), per a 2026 article; the company does not state this.

identity.visual_style: Terminal style labels such as // ATTACK and // PROTECT

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative literary name suits a protect the jewel framing and the dev style site fits developers, but the name is easy to misspell and no outside brand coverage was found.

outcome_analysis: Silmaril is a two person Spring 2026 security startup with no exit and unverified funding. It enters a space where funded rivals shipped similar runtime protection in the same quarter, so differentiation depends on independently validated detection performance.
notes: Funding aggregators disagree and no company or press source confirms any round, so no round is recorded. Conflicting aggregators: Dealroom $125K seed, FundedIQ $500K pre-seed June 2026 (also names an unrelated founder), VCBacked undisclosed. Education of founders not found. Undated competitor sources omitted from the list: Zenity.
